misleading_risk: Real risks in the proposal as written (all avoided in the refined version): (1) 'show the first categories entry as the task' puts a meaning on a free-form field. Schema categories are plain strings, up to 6, 30 characters each. The six seed manifests use 'cell tracking', 'TrackMate', 'experimental design', 'diagnostics', 'testing', 'example', 'registration'. Nobody wrote 'this is the scientific task', so the site would be inventing it. (2) Quickstart steps copied from READMEs into seed drafts. The CellTracksColab README step 'paths start with /content/gdrive/MyDrive/' is a Colab step, but the page's single quickstart list sits next to desktop tiles and the desktop boilerplate. Steps that nobody ran would also be shown as 'from the author'. (3) A verification or 'Verified' line beside the download. verified_on holds a date but no operating system, and benchmark section 3 wants 'which system'. Wording must stay the existing status text, with no OS claim, and the pip block must not imply the PyPI version equals the release shown above it. (4) Side finding that shows why limitations must come from authors: the GuessTheCondition README (line 49) says 'Intel Macs are not' supported, yet the page offers an Intel .pkg button. That belongs to another gap, but it is the kind of unverified claim the site already makes. (5) 'First-run steps: not stated by the author' on every page would be true but tells visitors nothing they can act on. The refined version sends that signal to authors instead.
refined_proposal:
Note on the two booleans: real=true and proportionate=true refer to the refined version below. The proposal as written (reorder, route chips, task chip, 'not stated' text, example_data, seed content, DESIGN edits) is not proportionate. The refined version is about 25 lines of code plus tests, with no new design. Build: 1. Status line in the Get-it block. In pages_apps.get_section, directly under h2 'Get it' and above the tiles, shown only when the app has a release and the installer route, add one lc-small line: release_line(app) + ' · ' + status_text(app). Example: 'v0.1.1 · 7 July 2026 · Community listing: not verified by a maintainer, and not a security audit'. Factor status_text out of the 'verified' expression in details_list (pages_apps.py:143-144) so the Details row and this line share one wording and nothing new is hand-written. Verified apps keep the existing 'Verified for X on date'. Tests: status_text for Community, Verified and an expired verification, and the line absent when there is no release. 2. Label the pip command. In get_section, put `

Advanced: install with pip

` before the lc-code div (pages_apps.py:103-104). Say nothing about versions or operating systems. Test: pip block has its own heading and is not inside the notebooks list. 3. Author nudge instead of page text. (a) Add `quickstart:` (3-6 short steps, plain text, desktop route) to the manifest example in content/submit.md. The example currently shows only name, summary, kind, hosts, distribution, license and icon, so authors who copy it never learn that quickstart exists (grep: no mention in content/, scripts/submit_app.py or .github/). (b) In catalogue.resolve, append a warning when the manifest has no quickstart, for example 'no quickstart: the page shows only the generic start-up text'. Warnings already reach build/problems.md and the ⚠ lines of the submission comment (submit_app.py), and publish.yml opens issues only for the problems section, so this creates no issue noise. No testing-section exemption; one rule. Tests: warning present without quickstart, absent with it. Also test using_section: steps rendered as an
    , `` in a step escaped, no
      when absent. That branch (pages_apps.py:113-114) has no test today, against AGENTS 'every new behaviour gets a test'. 4. Keep the generic boilerplate in using_section. It is true for these apps: every app's app/menuinst/Welcome.ipynb is the launcher that lists the notebooks with 'Open the notebook' buttons. It is not a runnable example, and VLab4Mic's Welcome descriptions are still the placeholder 'This notebook ... is for ...', so quickstart must come from the authors. 5. Optional, only if the owners want it now: `example_data`, an array of 1-3 {label, https url} in the schema (a new $def, because $defs/link only accepts colab.research.google.com), rendered in Using it as 'Try it with: ' through esc and the existing external-link handling. Only CellTracksColab has a downloadable dataset (Zenodo 8420011 and 8413510). The GuessTheCondition demo experiment, the NucleiSky crop demo and the Playground test data are made by tools or code, so a quickstart step names them in plain text. Do not start with this field; start with the quickstart content. 6. DESIGN.md: no change to row 18, because no header chips are added. Add one short row under 'Every page' or 'Buttons' saying the Get-it block shows version, date and tier sentence as lc-small helper text above the tiles, and the pip command has its own h3. Drop or defer: - Do not reorder the page. Keep 'Get it' directly under the header. Moving it below Works with, Produces and the screenshot contradicts the benchmark's own 'One prominent download or launch action' and 'the action to obtain the app should remain obvious'. Measured: Mac and Windows tiles at y=383 today would drop past y~1000. 5 of 6 apps have 0 screenshots and the sixth is a banner. Works with and Produces (G1/G2) do not exist yet. When G1/G2 land, add them as compact lines between lead and Get it, not the screenshot. - Do not add route chips (cards.route_badges) to the header. The Playground header at 390 px already wraps 6 chips, and the routes are listed one block below. The only case for chips is mobile Colab discoverability (Colab block at y=1274 at 390x844). Revisit after the status line lands. - Do not add a 'task' chip from categories. The summary is the one-sentence task by schema. If a task is wanted, show all categories as neutral topic tags, not as 'the task'. - Do not show 'First-run steps: not stated by the author' on the page. - Seed manifests: add quickstart text only as clearly marked drafts for the owners, only from steps verified against the README (desktop route), and do not treat it as site content. Not closable by this repository: the acceptance test 'Start an app for the first time -> runnable first example' stays unmet until the app owners add quickstart steps (and a dataset link where one exists) in their own repositories.
evidence:
Verified on the built site (http://localhost:8765/apps/nucleisky/, Playwright at 1280x800): h1 y=160, 'Get it' 383, 'Notebooks to open in your browser' 785, pip block 971, About 1064, screenshot 1180, Using it 1779, All downloads 1968 (the only 'Version 0.1.1, released 7 July 2026' text), Details 2568. At 390x844 the Colab block starts at y=1274. The auditor's numbers are accurate.

Real parts of the gap:
- Version and date are not beside the tiles: the buttons show only 'Windows installer / 303 MB · .exe'.
- The 'Community' chip is a bare span (cards.badge, cards.py:32-35) with no explanation; the meaning is in Details > Status.
- The pip div (pages_apps.py:104) follows the notebooks list directly with no heading, so it sits under 'Notebooks to open in your browser'.
- All 6 snapshots have quickstart=None; grep finds 'quickstart' only in pages_apps.py:113-114 and the schema. It is not in content/submit.md, scripts/submit_app.py or .github/. No test covers that branch. tests/test_site.py, test_audit.py and test_catalogue.py contain nothing for using_section.

Where the auditor over-reaches:
- Order. The current order already puts the download at the top (the screenshot above shows the tiles above the fold). Only NucleiSky has a screenshot and it is a banner. Works with and Produces are not built.
- Header chips. Playground at 390 px already shows 6 chips.
- Categories. They are free-form strings, so calling the first one 'the task' is not supported.
- The boilerplate is true. I read all six app/menuinst/Welcome.ipynb files. Each is the launcher that lists the notebooks with 'Open the notebook' buttons. It is a launcher, not a worked example, and VLab4Mic's descriptions are still the placeholder 'This notebook ... is for ...'.

Auditor's example-data claims checked and correct:
- CellTracksColab README line 246 gives Zenodo 8420011 and 8413510.
- GuessTheCondition README line 61 has the 'Create a demo experiment' tool.
- NucleiSky docs/2D/workflow.md:15 has generate_random_crop.
- Playground README line 26 has 'Make test data'.
- Only CellTracksColab has a downloadable dataset.
- quickstart steps are plain text through esc, so a link needs its own field.

The seed manifests are marked 'DRAFT for the app owners' and are loaded only via --manifest-dir (fetch_catalogue.py:3,19). Only LabConstrictor-Playground has a labconstrictor-app.yaml in its clone. Catalogue warnings so far come only from bad icons. publish.yml:69 opens an issue only for the problems section, not for warnings.

Other findings:
- The GuessTheCondition README (line 49) says Intel Macs are not supported, but the page offers an Intel .pkg button (site/apps/guessthecondition). This is an unverified OS claim, outside G4.
- The page now repeats the version in All downloads and in Details > Latest release. The status line would be a third place, so it should share the formatting helpers rather than be a new string.
